# 34 Describing situations

## A  Dialogues commenting on situations

> **Mary:** It's such a cold day. I wish I could **get out of** the bike ride Jack's planned. Lavoid doing something that you should do, often by giving an excuse]
> **Bill:** Why don't you suggest cancelling it? I'm sure the others would also prefer not to go in weather like this.
> **Sandy:** I have identical twins, Flora and Florence, in my class - I always **mix** them **up**. [confuse two people or things by thinking that one person or thing is the other person or thing]
> **Mike:** Yes, I **muddle** them **up** too. It doesn't help that their names are so similar. [confuse two people or things in your mind]
> **Meg:** I really don't like sharing an office with Sue - she thinks the whole world **revolves around** her and her insignificant problems. [thinks she's more important than anyone else]
> **Anna:** Yes, I know. I think she is one of the most self-centred people I've ever met.
> **John:** We've been **running up against**' quite a lot of problems here recently.
> **Rita:** I know. As soon as we deal with one problem, another immediately **crops up**' and I now feel I can't **bank on**? things **turning out*** well in the end.

## Exercises

### 34.1 Match the statements on the left with a suitable response on the right.
1. I'm so worried about what Jim is doing. {__}
2. All the pages are in the wrong order in this report. {__}
3. Sometimes the printer will only print black and white. {__}
4. I need you here next Monday. {__}
5. I do hope the bus arrives on time. {__}
6. I feel so angry about what's happened {__}

- I've run up against that problem too.
- I know, but I'm sure everything will turn out all right in the end.
- I wouldn't bank on it.
- I know, but try to rise above it.
- I must have mixed/ muddled them up. Sorry.
- OK. I'll see if I can get out of my trip to London.
